speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, such as whether there are scales, crusts, or pustules? Is this area itchy, painful, or just visually concerning?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the family history of psoriasis is significant. Since the rash worsens in cold weather and presents as red and scaly, could you clarify if there is any family history of atopic dermatitis or asthma as well? Additionally, has your baby been diagnosed with eczema or been prescribed any steroids for the rash before?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: TST (Mantoux Skin Test) and Quantiferon Gold. REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photos of the scalp and forehead lesions to assess for crusting or satellite lesions.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (infantile crusted/scalp involvement) or severe seborrheic dermatitis (given the "greasy yellow scales" and cold weather exacerbation, though the TB claim is highly suspect and likely a misdiagnosis given the age and lack of systemic symptoms). Given the family history of psoriasis and the specific description, we must rule out a psoriasiform reaction to an infection first.

Wait, let me re-evaluate based on the "greasy yellow scales" in an infant. This is classic for Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap), but the cold weather worsening and family history of psoriasis suggest a possible overlap or misdiagnosis. The previous doctor's claim of TB is extremely unlikely for this
